items.name: Ocean Prime
items.blurb: Polished surf-and-turf — seafood, prime steaks and classic cocktails with Seaport Boulevard water views.

items.name: Bar Mezzana
items.blurb: Coastal Italian in the South End — fresh crudo, homemade pasta and a standout wine list.

items.name: Nebo Cucina & Enoteca
items.blurb: Open, casual Italian — pizza, pasta and seafood; great for big groups or bellying up to the bar.

items.name: Committee
items.hours: Dinner nightly to late; lunch Mon–Fri; brunch Sat–Sun
items.blurb: Lively harborside Greek meze, shareable plates and creative cocktails.

items.name: High Street Place
items.blurb: Downtown food hall with 20+ vendors under one roof — fast, flexible, something for everyone.

items.name: Row 34
items.blurb: Classic New England raw bar and a funky craft-beer program — the closest serious sit-down to the EBC.

items.name: Mooo....
items.blurb: Modern steakhouse a one-minute walk from the EBC — prime cuts and an award-winning wine list.

items.name: Boqueria
items.blurb: Barcelona-style tapas, Spanish wines and craft cocktails; late-night bites on weekends.

items.name: Woods Hill Pier 4
items.blurb: Farm-to-table, sustainably sourced New American on the water at Pier 4.

items.name: The Nautilus Pier 4
items.hours: Dinner nightly; bar to midnight; lunch Sat–Sun
items.blurb: New England coastal cuisine meets Asian street food — a shared-plates, late-night vibe on the harbor.

items.name: Davio's Seaport
items.hours: Lunch Mon–Fri; dinner nightly; brunch Sat–Sun
items.blurb: Northern Italian steakhouse — aged steaks and handmade pasta on Fan Pier.

items.name: Coquette
items.blurb: Mediterranean raw bar and Capri-style pizzas inside the Omni Boston Hotel at the Seaport.

items.name: Trillium Brewing — Fort Point
items.blurb: Fort Point taproom and full restaurant from Boston's favorite craft brewery.

items.name: Harpoon Brewery & Beer Hall
items.blurb: Iconic Boston brewery and beer hall — fresh-pulled pretzels and a huge beer list.

items.name: The Barking Crab
items.blurb: Festive, tented harborside clam shack on Fort Point Channel — quintessentially Boston.

items.name: Legal Harborside
items.blurb: Legal Sea Foods' three-floor flagship at Liberty Wharf, with a retractable-roof rooftop bar.

items.name: Flour Bakery + Café
items.blurb: Joanne Chang's beloved original bakery — pastries, sandwiches and great coffee.

items.name: Rooftop at The Envoy
items.blurb: Seaport rooftop with skyline and harbor views — heated igloos in winter, atop The Envoy Hotel.

items.name: Lucky's Lounge
items.blurb: Retro Fort Point lounge with live music and Sinatra Sundays — find the unmarked basement door.

items.name: Yankee Lobster Co.
items.blurb: Family-run fish market and casual seafood counter — a no-frills local institution.

items.name: Maple & Ash
items.blurb: Glamorous wood-fired steakhouse and raw bar from chef Danny Grant — prime cuts, seafood towers and a buzzy cocktail scene.

items.name: The Block at Woods Hill
items.blurb: Woods Hill's farm-to-table small-plates and wine spot beside its Pier 4 flagship — same sustainable sourcing, more relaxed.

items.name: SAVR
items.blurb: Spirited New American bistro at the St. Regis Residences — steaks, pasta and a raw bar across two waterfront decks.

items.name: Mr. H
items.blurb: Relaunched in July 2026 as a 1940s-Shanghai-style salon — sushi-led menu, a big cocktail program and a late-night DJ lounge in Park Lane Seaport (COJE, sister of Coquette and Lolita).

items.name: Island Creek Raw Bar
items.blurb: Fully outdoor seasonal raw bar from Island Creek Oysters — just-shucked oysters, chilled seafood and cocktails on Harbor Way.

items.name: Cisco Brewers Seaport
items.blurb: Nantucket's Cisco Brewers' seasonal outdoor beer garden — a tented yard with live music, lawn games and reservable beach shacks.

items.name: Mastro's Ocean Club
items.blurb: Glamorous Fan Pier steakhouse and seafood — prime cuts, towering shellfish and live music with harbor views.

items.name: Empire
items.blurb: Sprawling pan-Asian restaurant and DJ lounge on Fan Pier — sushi, dumplings and late-night energy.

items.name: Serafina Seaport
items.blurb: Waterfront Italian on Fan Pier — wood-fired pizzas, handmade pasta and a harbor-view patio.

items.name: Tuscan Kitchen Seaport
items.blurb: Rustic Tuscan cooking with house-made pasta and 300+ wines, plus the ground-floor Bar Toscana.

items.name: Lakon Paris Patisserie
items.blurb: French patisserie and café on the Seaport's Autumn Lane — croissants, viennoiserie and espresso.

items.name: Blue Bottle Coffee
items.blurb: Minimalist specialty-coffee café in the Seaport — single-origin pour-overs, espresso and pastries.

items.name: Elephantine Bakery
items.blurb: European-style bakery and café in Fort Point — pastries, fresh bread and a light lunch menu.

items.name: Smith & Wollensky
items.blurb: Classic American steakhouse at Atlantic Wharf on Fort Point Channel — dry-aged beef and a clubby bar.

items.name: Abe & Louie's
items.blurb: Back Bay steakhouse institution across from the Boston Public Library — prime steaks and a power-lunch scene.

items.name: The Vermilion Club
items.hours: Lunch Mon–Fri; dinner Mon–Sat; closed Sun
items.blurb: Chef John Fraser's contemporary steakhouse at Winthrop Center — refined cuts and cocktails downtown.

items.name: Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steakhouse
items.blurb: Grand waterfront steakhouse in the Seaport — prime steaks, seafood towers and an extensive wine list.

items.name: Grill 23 & Bar
items.blurb: Long-running Back Bay steakhouse in a grand former bank hall — prime beef and a serious wine cellar.

items.name: TABLE by Jen Royle
items.hours: Dinner Wed–Sat; Sunday Supper; closed Mon–Tue
items.blurb: Chef Jen Royle seats everyone together at communal tables for a multi-course, family-style Italian prix-fixe feast in the North End.

items.name: Little Sage
items.blurb: Chef Tony Susi's intimate North End spot for handcrafted pastas and oven-roasted Italian dishes — a revival of his 1990s restaurant Sage.

items.name: Neptune Oyster
items.hours: Daily from 11am; walk-ins only, no reservations
items.blurb: Tiny, beloved North End raw bar famous for its hot-buttered lobster roll and pristine oysters — expect a wait, no reservations.

items.name: Regina Pizzeria
items.blurb: The original 1926 North End brick-oven pizzeria on a tiny side street — often cited as Boston's most famous pizza, and worth the line.

items.name: Sunny Girl
items.blurb: Chef-driven North End café beloved for inventive breakfast sandwiches on house-made English muffins.

items.name: Galleria Umberto
items.hours: Mon–Sat 11am–2:30pm (lunch & cash only; closes when sold out); closed Sun
items.blurb: Legendary cash-only, lunch-only counter slinging thick Sicilian squares and arancini for a few dollars until it sells out — a James Beard 'America's Classic'.

items.name: The Red Fox
items.blurb: A dim, sultry North End spot for handmade pasta and nostalgic martinis — with the hidden Extra Dirty Cocktail Club behind a curtain in back.

items.name: Parla
items.hours: Daily to midnight; dinner from 4:30pm; weekend brunch
items.blurb: Intimate, speakeasy-style den of inventive cocktails and modern Italian small plates on Hanover Street.

items.name: Farmacia
items.blurb: A nine-seat, apothecary-inspired bar serving a ticketed, multi-cocktail tasting 'experience' — book well ahead.

items.name: Extra Dirty Cocktail Club
items.blurb: A 20-seat hidden cocktail bar tucked behind a curtain at the back of The Red Fox — theatrical, award-winning mixology (Boston Magazine's Best New Bar, 2025).

items.name: Hawksmoor Boston
items.hours: Mon from 5pm; Tue–Sat from noon; Sun roast from 11:45am
items.blurb: London's celebrated charcoal-grill steakhouse, newly opened (September 2026) on the Fort Point Channel — literally steps from the EBC — with sub-zero martinis, a waterfront terrace, British Sunday roasts and two private dining rooms.

items.name: Fox & the Knife
items.blurb: Karen Akunowicz's Modena-inspired enoteca in South Boston — handmade pastas, aperitivo spritzes and a deep Italian wine and amaro list.

items.name: Bar Volpe
items.blurb: Karen Akunowicz's Southern Italian follow-up to Fox & the Knife — house-made pastas, wood-fired seafood, two bars with a deep amaro list, and a pastificio selling fresh pasta to go.

items.name: Somaek
items.blurb: Jamie Bissonnette's homestyle Korean spot in Downtown Crossing — banchan, seafood pajeon, galbi and a soju-and-makgeolli bar — on the NYT 2024 list of the 50 best US restaurants.

items.name: Mooncusser
items.hours: Tasting menu Tue–Sat 5–9pm; Moon Bar downstairs till late; closed Sun–Mon
items.blurb: Chef Carl Dooley's globally inspired, seafood-focused tasting menu upstairs in Back Bay, with the casual Moon Bar downstairs for à la carte plates and cocktails.

items.name: Zurito
items.blurb: With only 60 seats and a prime Beacon Hill location, the restaurant fills up fast, and the menu style leads to lingering at the bar with a view of the street, hanging legs of jamon, and a small, buzzy room

items.name: Institute of Contemporary Art
items.blurb: Cutting-edge contemporary art on the Seaport waterfront — painting, sculpture, film and photography.

items.name: Flight Club Boston
items.blurb: Upscale social darts with elevated food and cocktails — tech-tracked games for rookies and pros alike.

items.name: Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum
items.blurb: Live-guided, interactive retelling of the 1773 revolt aboard restored tall ships — throw the tea overboard.

items.name: SPIN Boston
items.hours: Tue–Sat afternoons to late; closed Sun–Mon
items.blurb: 20 ping-pong tables, a full bar and 15,000 sq ft of social energy — steps from the EBC.

items.name: New England Aquarium
items.blurb: Four-story Giant Ocean Tank, penguins, sharks and a touch tank — a global leader in marine conservation.

items.name: Puttshack Boston
items.blurb: Tech-enabled mini golf with auto-scoring balls, shareable plates and craft cocktails near Pier 4.

items.name: JFK Presidential Library & Museum
items.blurb: Relive the Kennedy era in I.M. Pei's striking waterfront building overlooking the Boston skyline.

items.name: Museum of Science
items.blurb: 700+ interactive exhibits, a planetarium and Omni theater spanning the Charles River dam.

items.name: Fenway Park
items.blurb: The oldest ballpark in the majors — catch a Red Sox game or tour this living piece of history.

items.name: Freedom Trail
items.address: Boston Common, 139 Tremont St, Boston, MA 02111
items.blurb: A 2.5-mile red-brick path past 16 Revolution-era sites, from Boston Common to Bunker Hill (~90 min).

items.name: Museum of Fine Arts
items.blurb: Boston's largest art museum — world-renowned Impressionist, Asian, Egyptian and early American collections.

items.name: Newbury Street
items.address: Newbury St, Back Bay, Boston, MA 02116
items.blurb: Boston's chic eight-block shopping stroll — boutiques, galleries, salons and sidewalk cafés in Back Bay.

items.name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
items.blurb: A Venetian palazzo wrapped around a skylit garden courtyard, filled with an eclectic European-to-Asian collection.

items.name: Quincy Market / Faneuil Hall
items.blurb: A bustling 1820s marketplace of food stalls, shops and street performers beside historic Faneuil Hall.

items.name: New England Aquarium Whale Watch
items.hours: Seasonal (mid-May–Nov); multiple departures daily; 3–4 hr cruises
items.blurb: A seasonal harbor excursion to Stellwagen Bank aboard high-speed catamarans with onboard naturalists — spot humpback, fin and minke whales. Departs Central Wharf by the Aquarium.

items.name: Omni Boston Hotel at the Seaport
items.blurb: AAA Four-Diamond flagship with a year-round heated rooftop pool and bar, spa and six dining venues.

items.name: Residence Inn Boston Downtown/Seaport
items.blurb: Suites with in-room kitchens and free hot breakfast — the closest hotel to the EBC, about a 5-minute walk.

items.name: The Westin Boston Seaport District
items.blurb: Large full-service hotel beside the convention center with an indoor pool and several restaurants and bars.

items.name: Renaissance Boston Seaport District
items.blurb: Waterfront-district hotel (formerly Renaissance Waterfront) with an indoor pool and the Capiz Bar & Lounge.

items.name: Element Boston Seaport District
items.blurb: Eco-focused extended-stay with in-room kitchens, free breakfast and an indoor pool.

items.name: InterContinental Boston
items.blurb: Luxury waterfront hotel on the Harbor with a 45-ft indoor lap pool, spa and floor-to-ceiling skyline views.

items.name: The Envoy Hotel, Autograph Collection
items.blurb: Design-forward boutique hotel with the popular Rooftop at The Envoy and intimate harbor views.

items.name: YOTEL Boston
items.blurb: Compact, tech-savvy 'cabin' rooms and the year-round Deck 12 rooftop bar with 360-degree views.

items.name: Aloft Boston Seaport District
items.blurb: Modern, music-loving select-service hotel with the WXYZ bar and lively social spaces.

items.name: Seaport Hotel Boston
items.blurb: Large waterfront convention hotel with a heated indoor pool, 24-hour Wave fitness club and harbor views.

items.name: Boston Harbor Hotel
items.blurb: Five-star landmark under the Rowes Wharf arch — a 60-ft indoor lap pool, spa and saunas on the harbor.

items.name: Boston Marriott Long Wharf
items.blurb: Waterfront Marriott beside the New England Aquarium — heated indoor pool and a 24-hour fitness center.

items.name: Boston Logan International Airport
items.blurb: Boston's main airport — about a 10–15 minute taxi ride or Silver Line (SL1) trip from the Seaport. Live arrival and departure status by terminal below (Logan has Terminals A, B, C and E — there is no Terminal D).

items.name: South Station
items.kind: Amtrak · commuter rail · Red & Silver lines
items.hours: Daily, early morning to late night
items.blurb: Boston's largest transit hub and the closest station to the EBC — about a 10-minute walk. Amtrak (including Acela), MBTA commuter rail, the Red Line, and the Silver Line straight to Logan.

items.name: North Station
items.kind: Amtrak · commuter rail · Green & Orange lines
items.hours: Daily, early morning to late night
items.blurb: North-side rail hub beneath TD Garden — Amtrak's Downeaster to Maine, MBTA commuter rail north and west, and the Green & Orange lines. Also reachable by the new Harbor Loop ferry from the Seaport.

items.name: Commonwealth Pier — Seaport Ferry
items.kind: MBTA Harbor Loop ferry (F10) · Seaport dock
items.blurb: The Seaport stop on the MBTA's year-round Harbor Loop ferry (route F10) — a short walk from the EBC, with water service to Logan Airport, Central Wharf (New England Aquarium) and Lovejoy Wharf at North Station.
